ety.text: Derived from Old Ruthenian москаль (moskalʹ), from a contraction of Ottoman Turkish مسقولو (moskovlu, “Russian”, literally “Muscovite”). Its recent negative association originated from referring to soldiers from the Imperial Russian Army, and later applied to the Soviet Army and Russians in general. By surface analysis, Москва (Moskva) + -аль (-alʹ).
